chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (revocation), and her waiting period is the nearer of the two periods.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a pregnant woman who is divorced according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a pregnant woman’s ʿiddah concludes upon childbirth, citing the principle of 'the nearer of the two periods' to resolve juristic debates regarding whether the waiting period is defined by the duration of pregnancy or the shorter of two potential cycles. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh to prioritize the actual event of delivery as the definitive marker for the end of marital status, ensuring clarity in lineage and remarriage eligibility.
